You guys & gals supporting titles such as this will only strengthen developers to keep making more.. and I truly, STRONGLY believe that we need more games, like THIS one.

Deceit is an asymmetrical multiplayer first-person horror game.
Innocents have to traverse three zones and escape through the safety hatch as the infected tries to kill them before they reach the end.
It was originally sold for 14,99€ and became free to play as the playerbase was really low.
Deceit has not a really huge playerbase nowadays but it is more or less stable (around 1000 as peak a day).
Voice chat is very important in this game, you need to convince people that you are innocent. Playing without a microphone puts you at a huge disadvantage, also you should be able to lie if you are the infected.
Deceit is unique and different from most games, it provides fun for a good amount of hours and it is also a good free alternative to Dead by Daylight.

**SYNOPSIS** The Game Master has kidnapped six players and locked them away in a remote location. Two out of the six players are infected and must kill the innocent players before they escape. The innocent players must escape the Game Masters arena while simultaneously trying to figure who the two infected players are.

This type of game is a classic "who is my enemy and who is my friend" because you truly cannot trust anyone in this game no matter what they say or do.

**CONS**
- Game sometimes lags in certain areas of the maps
- As of now, 3/21/2017, there are only two maps and they get boring pretty fast
- Cameras are WAY too powerful against the infected when they are in Terror Form
- Asian players invade the NA servers so you may get into a game where no one speaks your language
- Some players go on shooting sprees to simply rank up their perks and it ruins the depth of the game
- Cosmetics. I added this because having very specific cosmetics that you unlock can ruin the fun for this type of game. The idea that everyone looks the same makes it difficult to differentiate between two characters which is fun. People can now just say, "OH IT'S THE GUY WITHOUT THE SHIRT AND THE GREEN ST. PATTY'S DAY HAT." and he becomes a SUPER easy target to find.
- YOU NEED A MICROPHONE TO PLAY EFFECTIVELY
- Alot of people play with their friends and only chat in discord or Teamspeak ruining the immersion.

**PROS**
- Every round feels "new" because of the new group of players you are playing with
- Dev's have been releasing updates pretty often to fix bugs amongst other things
- Decent price for a decent game
- Have only had game crash twice out of the 21 hours i've played

Would I recommend this game? Yes. Does it have potential? Yes. Will I continue playing it? Yes.

I used to love playing Deceit, it was Unique and the whole reason I got it was because I stumbled across some Youtubers playing it. It had a unique system.

Innocent:
You pull a lever and either stand in an objective ring or shoot/knife targets for items.
There was also the double objective, a test of trust depending on the item ( shotgun, lethal or inspection kit)
Then when the lights went out hell breaks loose and half the time yer panicking to get the fuses in before you get killed.
Then once all fuses are in you have to run like mad to the next area and the game flowed wonderfully from area to area.
When you voted you shot/stabbed people, very satisfying when you are absolutely sure the person you downed is a Terror.

Infected:
Drink three bars of blood (3 double bags or 6 half bags) to unlock Terror Form
Each Terror type has specialties. Experiment (temporary body double), Yeti (temporary damage immunity), Werewolf (Howl disorientation) and Vampire (bat getaway).
You could play the short game if your partner was good enough and end everyone in the first round, or the long game and try to buddy with the innocents and make it a 2v2 and then end the game at the last area of a map. But then they can still get away too.

Deceit was a pulse pounding HORROR game that was all about lying. It was fluid and beautifully gory. 

Not to mention that the perk tree was fun because you could literally choose a different build as you gained perk points. And it reset every season making it all the more fun.

You never knew for sure who was gonna win and it was FUN.

THE LORE

Part of the fun was always being able to talk, the darkness of the maps, the fact that you don't know if you are innocent or infected until you are in the "game" and go running around.

Deceit is a game about 6 survivors who wake up. Two of them have contracted a disease that makes them thirsty for blood. The two infected have to work together to kill the other four innocent players. They can achieve this by drinking blood bags to fill their "blood meter". Once their blood meter is full, they can transform into a "terror" - a terrifying monster that can kill survivors in one hit if they don't have armor. 

Every minute or so, a blackout will happen, when the infected can transform into their terrifying forms, and the most dreaded phase for the innocents. They can either survive for about a minute before the power comes back online anyway, or find 2-3 fuses to set the timer to ten seconds. 

Deceit is a game about deceiving others if you are the infected, and knowing whether or not you can trust your "teammates" around you. In this game, you cannot trust anyone.

Sometimes the matches can become repetitive, though. But I guess that would apply to basically every single game with a multiplier mode. 

Overall, great game, and would recommend it to everyone! :)

This game is Trouble in Terrorist Town spliced with Dead by Daylight in a nutshell. As the game implies, you must overcome trust issues. 
As the innocent, you move quickly and get geared up for the inevitable while keeping an eye on suspicious players. 
As the infected, deception is your best friend. If you confuse a group of innocents long enough, you'll buy yourself enough time to keep them divided before you go in for the kill. 

Is it worth it? ABSOLUTELY. It's a game that thrives on community. It's well balanced, its addicting, and every game presents a new challenge and dynamic based on the players around you. The developers have been implementing gameplay tweaks and updates since its release. The only big thing that is left is optimization and this game will be perfect. $15 is a great value for a game like this.
